research_project.title: A Critical Reflection on How Questioning Strategies Can Be Used to Facilitate High Quality Teaching and Learning in a Bilingual Primary School Setting

context.researcher_position: insider-researcher at the school being studied

timeframe.data_collection: 5 weeks (Week 1: questionnaires; Weeks 2-3: interviews; Weeks 4-5: analysis)

participants.description: 7 teachers completed the questionnaire; 2 of those 7 (Teacher A, Teacher B) also completed semi-structured interviews
participants.characteristics: All with ≥1 full academic year teaching across both English-medium and Chinese-medium lessons

research_questions: What gap, if any, exists between teachers' stated beliefs about questioning and their reported classroom practice?
Does open-ended questioning work equitably in a bilingual primary classroom?
How does English-medium questioning shape which learners appear to understand and which do not?

significant_findings.title: Structural Belief–Practice Gap
significant_findings.description: 5 of 7 teachers showed mismatch between espoused belief and reported practice regarding questioning

significant_findings.title: Open-Ended Questioning as Participation Filter
significant_findings.description: 5 of 7 teachers described open-ended questions as answering by same few English-confident pupils

significant_findings.title: English-Medium Questioning Conflates Production with Understanding (BICS–CALP)
significant_findings.description: 3 of 7 teachers described pupils understanding concepts in Chinese but unable to produce answers in English

significant_findings.title: Absence of Shared Institutional Framework
significant_findings.description: 0 of 7 teachers referenced any formal questioning framework or school-level guidance

significant_findings.title: Personal Practice Change
significant_findings.description: Mo changed personal classroom response to pupil silence after research findings

significant_findings.title: Mixed Wait-Time Effects
significant_findings.description: Wait-time effects inconsistent across teachers - context-dependent rather than universal

significant_findings.title: Methodological Rigour
significant_findings.description: Research demonstrates strong methodological approach through triangulation, documented reliability thresholds, and reflexivity
